explain: _in_ takes the ablative to say where something is. _Italiā_ is the ablative singular of _Italia_ (first declension: -a becomes -ā). _Rōma_ is the subject and _est_ means 'is'.
distractors: _sunt_ means 'are'. _Rōma_ is one city, so the verb is _est_.
The grammar is fine, but _Graeciā_ means 'in Greece'.
Subject and place are swapped: that says 'Italy is in Rome'.

explain: Same pattern as before: _in_ + ablative (_Eurōpā_). Notice that _Italia_ (subject, nominative) and _Italiā_ (ablative) differ only by the macron, so macrons carry real information.
distractors: Swapped: that says 'Europe is in Italy'.

explain: _Graecia_ is singular, so the verb is _est_ ('is').
_Aegyptus_ looks masculine (-us) but names a country, which is grammatically feminine. It doesn't matter yet: the verb is still _est_. _Āfricā_ is the ablative after _in_.
distractors: Swapped: 'Africa is in Egypt'. (_Aegyptō_ is the ablative of _Aegyptus_.)

explain: _Aegyptus_ belongs to the second declension, so its ablative singular ends in -ō: _in Aegyptō_. First-declension words like _Italia_ end in -ā. Latin has no articles, so 'the Nile' is just _Nīlus_.
distractors: That says 'The Nile is in Italy'.

explain: _Germānia_ is first declension, so the ablative is _Germāniā_.
distractors: That says 'The Rhine is in Gaul'.

explain: The city name _Athēnae_ is grammatically plural (like English 'the Netherlands'), so the verb is _sunt_ ('are') even though English says 'Athens is'.
distractors: _Athēnae_ is plural in form, so the verb must be plural: _sunt_.
Swapped: 'Greece is in Athens'. (_Athēnīs_ is the ablative plural.)

en: Rome and Athens are in Europe.
explain: Two subjects joined by _et_ ('and') take a plural verb: _sunt_.
distractors: Rōma et Athēnae in Eurōpā est.
Rōma et Athēnae in Āfricā sunt.
That says they are in Africa.
Rōma et Athēnae in Graeciā sunt.
That puts Rome in Greece as well.

en: Italy and Greece are in Europe.
explain: Two subjects, so _sunt_. The place after _in_ is ablative: _Eurōpā_. (_in_ + accusative, as in _Eurōpam_, would mean 'into Europe', movement towards.)
distractors: Italia et Graecia in Eurōpā est.
Italia et Graecia in Āfricā sunt.
That says they are in Africa.
Italia et Graecia in Eurōpam sunt.
_in_ + accusative means 'into'. To say where, use the ablative: _Eurōpā_.

explain: _nōn_ ('not') usually stands right before the word it negates, most often the verb: _nōn est_.
distractors: Without _nōn_ this says 'Egypt IS in Europe'.
That says 'Egypt is not in Africa'.

explain: Same pattern: _nōn_ before the verb. A true statement makes a good sentence to repeat to yourself.
distractors: Without _nōn_ this says 'Italy IS in Africa'.
That says 'Italy is not in Europe' (false!).
